Part II develops the computational, statistical, and artificial-intelligence toolkit required for research at the economics–computer science interface.

It progresses from reproducible research computing through statistical and causal learning, deep learning, optimisation, reinforcement learning, multi-agent learning, and foundation models.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Relationship with Part I

Some subjects intentionally appear in both parts at different levels. Part I uses algorithms, optimisation, networks, and learning to understand economic institutions and strategic systems. Part II develops those methods at greater computational and research depth.
:::

## Part II outcome

The goal is research-level fluency with the computational methods increasingly used in algorithmic economics, computational social science, market design, digital economics, and AI-mediated economic systems.
